mine: to anoint a most holy place
note: qodesh qodashim ("holy of holies") elsewhere always denotes a sacred place or objects, never a person; KJV's capitalised "most Holy" invites a reading as the Messiah.

kjv: unto the Messiah the Prince [shall be] seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks
mine: until an anointed one, a prince, there shall be seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it (Jerusalem) shall be built again
note: mashiah nagid lacks the article ("an anointed one, a prince"), and the Masoretic accent (atnach) ends the clause after "seven weeks"; KJV joins 7+62 = 69 weeks to the coming of "the Messiah", the basis of the classic Christian chronology. Context: seven weeks to an anointed prince; then sixty-two weeks of rebuilding (MT accents) (low confidence). The WLC's atnach divides after 'seven weeks', 'an anointed one, a prince' lacks the article, and 9:26 places an anointed one 'cut off' after the 62 weeks, suggesting two figures. But Theodotion and the Vulgate join both numbers to the anointed one, the accents are mediaeval, and major versions split. The CT follows its source's accents with low confidence. Other possible meanings: (1) 'unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks' (69 weeks to the Messiah) — Theodotion, Vulgate, KJV, NIV, NASB, CSB, NET, the classic Christian chronology ending in Jesus; (2) the anointed one after seven weeks as Cyrus (Isa 45:1), Zerubbabel or Joshua the high priest — commentators following the accents, cf. ESV, NRSV, NJPS.

kjv: shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself
mine: an anointed one shall be cut off and shall have nothing
note: ve'en lo means "and there is nothing/no one for him", not "not for himself" (a vicarious reading); the anointed one, without article, is often identified with the high priest Onias III.

kjv: for the overspreading of abominations he shall make [it] desolate
mine: on the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate
note: kenaf shiqqutsim meshomem is "on the wing (pinnacle) of abominations, a desolator"; the phrase underlies "abomination of desolation" (Dan 11:31, 12:11; Mark 13:14), which KJV's wording obscures.
